sheets.note: Capital work-in-progress and intangibles under development, project by project - each park's total is compared live with Zoho's ledgers of the two accounts.

ties.label: Capital work-in-progress (transmission line and MCR) = CWIP in the Balance Sheet
Intangibles under development (pure services + boundary wall) = Balance Sheet line

live.keeps: Zoho has two ledger accounts for this sheet - Capital Work in Progress and Intangible Asset Under Development - and no park column. Its FY26 books were rebuilt at the year end, so almost all of the money arrived through clean-up journals of 31-Mar-2026 that empty an old ledger account into the new one, and the old account's NAME says the park ('Land Lease Dechu', 'Connectivity Charges Kolayat NPD', 'Civil Work Napasar'); the auditors' own journals and the bills (project, narration, location) say it too. Every line of the two ledgers is given the park its text names, and each park is compared with the sum of its three signed columns (pure services, boundary wall and road, transmission line and MCR). The split of a park over those three columns is the auditors' own classification - Zoho only has the two accounts, and one journal (SJ-1130) moves Rs 12,01,37,795 from CWIP to IAUD without saying park by park - so the three columns are not compared one by one. A handful of lines name no park in Zoho: where the signed sheet places them is listed below. Checked on the real books on 17-Oct-2026: both ledgers add up to the Trial Balance to the paisa, and 16 of the 18 parks agree with the sheet to within Re 1; Kolayat and Bhamatsar differ by Rs 84,000 each way, one bill that Zoho books to Kolayat and the sheet counts under Bhamatsar.

sheets.note: Closing stock, item by item - compared live with Zoho's Inventory Valuation Summary.

ties.label: Value as per trial balance = inventories

live.keeps: Zoho's Inventory Valuation Summary (its stock summary) is read as at the balance sheet date, and every signed row is paired with the Zoho line of the same item by name, quantity and value (an item can have an old SKU and a '_New' one, so it can stand on several rows and several lines). The 'Usage unit' of each row is checked against the unit of that item in Zoho's item list (matched by SKU; the stock summary itself leaves the unit blank). The 'New Rate' column is empty on the signed sheet, so there is nothing in it to check. Checked on the real books on 17-Oct-2026: all 246 rows and both totals agreed with Zoho to the paisa. The foot of the sheet works out its 'Difference' as the Trial Balance less the items less 'NPD Panchu Purchase' (4,81,953), and that is checked live too. The two NPD Panchu items (ABT meter, Raw material for Column) are already among the item rows - in Zoho's valuation as well - so the whole gap between the ledger and the items is 9,14,700.60, all of it in the Inventory Asset account; the tables below show what that account is made of, read from its ledger.

sheets.note: Customer-wise ageing of trade receivables, 31 March 2026. Every customer's closing balance is checked live against Zoho, and so are the year's invoicing and receipts and the age buckets Less than 6 months, 6 months to 1 year and Older than 1 year (the last one against the three typed columns added up). Zoho cannot split the older balances into 1-2, 2-3 and over 3 years.

ties.label: Closing balance, all customers = trade receivables

live.keeps: The age buckets are not a Zoho report: they are worked out from what Zoho does give - the customer balances on 31 March 2025, 30 September 2025 and 31 March 2026 and the sales (invoices less credit notes) of each half of the year - taking the oldest invoices as paid first, which is how the auditors aged the sheet. A manual journal that debits a customer is not an invoice, so Sales by Customer does not see it: it is told from the change of the customer's balance and aged by the half of the year it falls in. A few customers still differ because the auditors adjusted them by hand: year-end journals that move a balance from one customer account to another (RAYS ROOFTOP SPV against RAYS O&M EXPERTS) and TDS they netted by hand; no rule can tell these from the books. '1 to 2 Years', '2 to 3 Years' and 'More than 3 Years' stay as signed and are compared together with the live 'older than 1 year'.

sheets.note: Vendor-wise ageing of trade payables, 31 March 2026. Every vendor's closing balance is checked live against Zoho, and so are the opening balance, Billed Amount, Paid Amount, the Vendor Code and the buckets Less than 1 year and Older than 1 year (the last one against the three typed columns added up). Two vendors that are retention money (Cyrun-Infra Projects LLP, Gurukripa Traders) are in no age bucket, as the auditors show them. MSME stays as signed. The three insurance policy lines (HDFC ERGO twice, ICICI Lombard) are not trade-payable vendors in Zoho: their closing balance is read from the insurer's own ledger entries (the payable side of the contact) - the ICICI Lombard line on its own, the two HDFC ERGO lines together, because Zoho books all of its bills at the Head Office. Their other columns stay as signed.

ties.label: Ageing buckets added up = trade payables (Note 9)

live.keeps: Opening balance and the age buckets are worked out from the Zoho ledger of the supplier accounts: the credit balance on 31 March 2025, and what is still unpaid of it after the year's payments, oldest first; the year's billing in that rule is Zoho's Billed Amount. Billed Amount and Paid Amount are compared with Zoho's Vendor Balance Summary: the year is the report up to 31 March 2026 less the report up to 31 March 2025. The Vendor Code is read from each vendor's own card in Zoho (the code is a custom field that no report gives): 40 cards per refresh until all 166 are known, then kept in Redis and read again after a week; a vendor whose card has not been read yet is simply not compared. Retention money (Cyrun-Infra Projects LLP, Gurukripa Traders: config/party_overrides.fy26.json) is listed with its balance but in no age bucket. The MSME flag stays as signed (the list is kept in config/party_rules.json: Zoho's Udyam fields are empty). '1-2 Yr.', '2-3 Yr.' and '>3 Yr' stay as signed and are compared together with the live 'older than 1 year'. The three insurance policy lines (HDFC ERGO twice, ICICI Lombard) are not trade-payable vendors in Zoho: their closing balance is read from the insurer's own ledger entries (the payable side of the contact) - the ICICI Lombard line on its own, the two HDFC ERGO lines together, because Zoho books all of its bills at the Head Office. Their other columns stay as signed.

sheets.note: Related-party transactions, party by party.

Account-wise detail behind the Balance Sheet notes, checked line by line against Zoho: customers, vendors, advances to suppliers, imprest, retention, loans, outstanding expenses, investments, tax balances, GST and the other ledger accounts. The fixed deposits and the accrued interest (bank by bank), the three security deposits, the PF employee / employer share, the advance and the payable of each insurer and the loan and the advance of RPE Energy Reserve are lines of their own too: Zoho keeps each of them in one account, the entries say which line they belong to. Compared in total, because Zoho cannot tell them apart: the staff imprest advances, the ESI employee / employer share, and the two HDFC ERGO payables (Rajasthan and Delhi). One thing stays as signed: the short / long-term split of the loans. The advances received from customers are read from the ledger of the account Advance from debtors, less the auditors' hand-netting.

live.keeps: What stays as signed: the short / long-term split of the loans. The list of advances from customers is read from Zoho (the ledger of the account Advance from debtors up to the balance sheet date, customer by customer, less the amounts the auditors netted by hand against the customers' invoices, plus the credit of a customer whose receivable is below zero) and checked line by line like the other lists. Read line by line, from the entries behind Zoho's one account: the fixed deposits and the accrued interest bank by bank (the bank is in the name of the old account on the clean-up journal of 31-Mar-2026, or in the text of the auditors' journal), the three security deposits, the PF employee / employer share (the payroll entry that says so, the rest is the employer share), and - by the Zoho account their entries sit in - the advance and the payable of HDFC ERGO and ICICI Lombard and the loan and the advance of RPE Energy Reserve. Compared in total, because Zoho does not hold them apart: the eleven staff imprest advances (the entries carry no name of the person), the employee and employer share of ESI, and the HDFC ERGO payables of Rajasthan and Delhi (all its bills are booked at the Head Office).
